title: Recovering each base chart from an etale descent quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a jointly surjective etale covering [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $f_i:X_i\to U_i$ schemes. Put $U_{ij}=U_i\times_SU_j$ and $R_{ij}=X_i\times_{U_i}U_{ij}$, with projection $p_i:R_{ij}\to X_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose given isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}:R_{ij}\simeq R_{ji}$ over $U_{ij}$ (with the base factors interchanged), restricting to the identity along $U_i\to U_{ii}$ and satisfying $\theta_{jk}\theta_{ij}=\theta_{ik}$ on every triple overlap. Form $V=\coprod_iX_i$, $R=\coprod_{i,j}R_{ij}$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and $s,t:R\to V$ with components $p_i$ and $p_j\theta_{ij}$. Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and $q:h_V\to F$ an etale surjective map satisfying $qs=qt$, such that the induced map $h_R\to h_V\times_Fh_V$ is an isomorphism. Write $q_i:h_{X_i}\to F$ for its restriction. Then the natural maps $a_i=(q_i,f_i):h_{X_i}\to F\times_Sh_{U_i}$ are isomorphisms. Their induced transition on $U_{ij}$ is exactly $\theta_{ij}$; the kernel pair identifies $X_i\times_FX_j$ with $R_{ij}$ with projections $p_i,p_j\theta_{ij}$, and $\{q_i\}$ is a jointly surjective etale covering of $F$.

source.place: Tags 02WW (spaces theorem-presentation) and 02WV (spaces lemma-when-it-works-it-works), presentation kernel-pair identity specialized to a scheme descent cocycle; explicit recovery of base charts by representable-sheaf gluing.

proof.text: Apply the proved component-kernel-pair lemma to the given coproducts with second projection θ_ij followed by p_ji. This supplies every displayed individual kernel-pair square.

If x,y:T→X_i have equal quotient section, use the component kernel-pair square for (i,i) to obtain r:T→R_ii with projections x and y. Equality f_i x=f_i y and the switched base-coordinate equation imply equality of the two b_ii coordinates of r. Normalization gives θ_ii r=r and hence x=y.

The equation qs=qt restricts along κ_ij to the relation needed by the chart-section-lifting lemma. Apply that lemma with the injectivity just proved to obtain chart sections with every prescribed quotient/base-coordinate pair. Together with injectivity and the pointwise product projections this makes each component of (q_i,f_i) bijective; the pointwise isomorphism criterion for natural transformations proves the chart isomorphisms.

Precomposing the quotient relation with r gives equal quotient sections for p_ij r and p_ji θ_ij r. If r' has switched base coordinates, equality of these quotient sections and injectivity for X_j identify the two X_j projections. The switched coordinate hypotheses identify the two b_ji projections, so the R_ji pullback property gives θ_ij r=r'. The converse follows directly from the relation.

For any a:h_T→F, the chart isomorphism identifies its pullback with h_(T×_S U_i). Explicitly use the inverse of (q_i,f_i) to define the map from T×_S U_i to X_i; transport the standard product pullback square through that isomorphism and the Yoneda product comparison. The projection to T is etale by base change from U_i→S. For each point z of T choose i and y∈U_i over its image in S; the scheme pullback has a point above (z,y). These projections jointly cover T and are exactly the required representing family.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0262, 02WV/02WW: restrict the kernel pair, normalize to prove injectivity, and use local lifts plus subcanonical fppf gluing for surjectivity. Recover the final atlas by base-changing the original U_i cover along T→S.

Step 1 (kernel pair restricted to R_ij) is correct: the coproduct components are disjoint, so r^-1(R_ab) is empty for (a,b)!=(i,j), and r factors through the open immersion. Step 2 (injectivity) is correct: in coordinates theta_ii sends (x,(u,w)) to (y,(w,u)) with f_i y=w, so f_i y=u forces w=u, and the diagonal normalization gives y=x. Step 3 is correct: lem-a1-representable-etale-fppf-local-lifting gives exactly the surjective etale v:P->T and the lift b. The P_j form an fppf cover (by etale-composition (1),(2) and the definition of etale). r_j is defined because b_j and u are S-maps. c_j=p_i theta_ji r_j satisfies f_i c_j=u_j and, by qs=qt, q_i c_j=z. Step 4 is correct: Step 2 gives compatibility, fppf covers are fpqc, and representable fpqc descent applies with no finiteness hypotheses. Uniqueness with targets S and U_i gives the S-map and f_i c=u, and the sheaf equalizer gives q_i c=z. Step 5 shows the transition equals theta_ij because a_j is bijective. Step 6 identifies P_i=P x_V X_i with T x_F X_i, shows it is etale, and shows the P_i jointly cover T; it correctly does not claim each q_i is surjective. Edge cases checked: empty I is vacuous; a single chart over S gives the identity; non-monomorphic U_i is handled by the diagonal-only use.
